messages:
maria-cs: Hey team — customer xyz@example[.]net reports their free trial was blocked during signup. They supplied a valid card and phone but they hit the trial hold. Can someone look? link to support ticket: https://redwood/support/CT-87421 :wave:

sara-support: I pulled the hold — system shows risk flags. Can you paste the signup metadata? IP, user agent, and email provider?

maria-cs: Here are the fields from the support form: 
- email: xyz@example[.]net (gmail-alike domain)
- ip: 45.77.23.12
- user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36
- card_last4: 4242
- phone: +1-415-555-0123
- promo: TRIAL50

fraud-bot: Auto-check results:
- score: 0.82 (threshold 0.6)
- flags: ip_proxy_detected, disposable_email_confidence=0.6, high_velocity_card_bin
- note: vpn_or_tor=true for IP 45.77.23.12

sara-support: Thanks. The bot is flagging ip_proxy and disposable email confidence borderline. The customer insists they're genuine. Do we have any signals to disprove proxy?

james-eng: Quick check — looked up IP on our geo lookup: ASN shows DigitalOcean (datacenter). Reverse DNS: no ptr. Not typical residential ISP. Also card BIN 424242 is a test/visa BIN commonly used in fraud attempts.

maria-cs: The customer says they used a coworker machine and 'forgot' to mention that's a cloud VM. They also uploaded a company ID in the ticket (scanned ID) and claim they need enterprise evaluation.

alan-ops: From ops perspective: we should require manual verification if proxy + disposable score > 0.5 and card bin suspicious. Standard playbook: ask for matching billing address + small $1 verification (authex).

sara-support: Agreed. I requested billing address and asked them to upload a selfie with ID and to confirm last 4 digits of card. Also suggested they add their corporate email if possible. Awaiting reply. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria-cs: Customer replied with a selfie+ID — the name matches account name. Billing address is a company HQ in SF. They provided a corporate invoice email as alt contact.

fraud-bot: Re-run after new evidence:
- score: 0.45
- flags: disposable_email_confidence=0.2, ip_proxy_detected (unchanged)
- comment: evidence reduced some risk but ip still suspicious.

james-eng: Important: proxy flag remains. However, product policy allows manual override when identity docs + billing match and customer is enterprise. We need 2-person approval (support lead + ops) and to log reason for compliance.

sara-support: @alan-ops can you approve manual trial grant? I'll attach all documents to ticket CT-87421.

alan-ops: I'm +1 for manual grant assuming we add controls: limit to single trial, no promo stacking, watch for abnormal API usage. Recommend setting soft rate limits and 30-day monitoring.

kevin-legal: Quick note from legal: keep copies of ID in secure ticketing storage, redact SSN. Also confirm customer's contract/terms acceptance for trial.

sara-support: Done. I've redacted SSN and stored artifacts per policy. Applying manual override now and setting account flags: trial_granted_manual=true, monitor_window=30d, max_req_per_min=20.

maria-cs: Customer notified and now has trial access. They said thanks and will schedule onboarding call. :tada:

sara-support: Closing loop — logged decision rationale in ticket: manual grant due to matching government ID + billing address + corporate invoice despite Datacenter IP. Controls: limited usage, 30-day monitoring, revoke if abusive. Marking thread resolved. 

maria-cs: Thanks all. Note for playbook: maybe we add a quick checklist for cloud-vm signups to speed these — lots of enterprise users can be on cloud IPs.\n
